_header: ===== cherrypick-pmcc — PMCC-99 deep-ITM covered calls on TQQQ (paper-only) =====
_what_this_is: Buy an 85-90-delta call at ~21 DTE (a stock substitute, NOT a LEAP), sell the ATM call nearest spot at ~7 DTE regardless of which side of spot it lands on. Since the 2026-08-23 redesign this is a single book (`control`) run across two symbols: TQQQ (American, physical-settlement ETF) and, added the same day, XSP (Mini-SPX, European, cash-settled broad-based index option). Same rules, two structurally different underlyings measured as separate populations — see the module CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-23 note. Mechanical entry, hold to the short's own expiration, then close both legs together. `tv_close_threshold`/`tv_managed_exit` remain as an advisor-tunable early-exit experiment, run only through the synthetic `advised:control` book. TQQQ's early assignment is REFUSED-around and MEASURED, never modelled — see the dividends block and the assignment_exposure_tv knob; XSP carries neither risk (see _settlement_style_note). Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or ~/.cherrypick/config/pmcc.json.
_symbols_note: TQQQ (Nasdaq-100 3x, American physical delivery) and XSP (Mini-SPX, European cash settlement), one book (`control`) since the 2026-08-23 redesign — both $1-or-finer strikes, weekly expirations. One position per (symbol, book) at a time — max_positions bounds the book to how many concurrent cycles it may hold, summed across symbols. A symbol not declared in settlement_style is refused at entry (unknown_settlement); TQQQ and XSP results are NOT interchangeable — different settlement mechanics and risk profile, directly comparable only as separate populations under the same rule set.
_occ_roots_note: The OCC root the provider admits per underlying. Leveraged ETFs split often, and a split leaves ADJUSTED roots (TQQQ1) sharing expiration dates with the standard root; only the configured root is priced, and an expiration listing only adjusted roots refuses `not_root_listed`. After a split, verify the standard root re-lists before resuming — and treat a split mid-position as a manual `--settle` plus a measurement break (unmodelled). XSP does not split, so its root is simply itself.
_settlement_style_note: How each symbol's expiring legs settle. TQQQ is `physical` — American delivery: an ITM short call hands over 100 short shares per contract at the settlement print, covered the NEXT session together with the long's sale (the combined disposal), so a Friday assignment carries short shares over the weekend. Delivered shares are booked at the SETTLEMENT SPOT, not the strike — the calendars decomposition, which keeps physical settlement exactly cash-plus-a-share-leg. XSP is `cash` — European exercise style, so it can ONLY be exercised at its own expiration: there is no early-assignment risk to refuse around (the dividends block below has no XSP entry and none is needed — `_entry_guards` in paper_loop.py only runs the ex-dividend check for `physical` symbols) and no delivered-share path ever fires for it (`assignment_from` is only called from the `physical` branch of `book.settle_expiring_legs`). `management.assignment_exposed` is likewise exempt for `cash` positions — see its docstring. A symbol declared as neither style is refused at entry.
_dividends_note: PHYSICAL-settlement symbols only. Entries whose short leg spans a declared ex-dividend date are REFUSED (ex_dividend_span): a short ITM call is really assigned at the close BEFORE the ex-date, and this module deliberately does not model early assignment. This check is skipped outright for `cash`-settled symbols (XSP) — a European option cannot be exercised early, so there is no ex-date question to answer, and XSP therefore needs NO entry in this block at all (dividend_coverage_ok/ex_date_in_span are simply never called for it; see _entry_guards in paper_loop.py). For physical symbols, dates are DECLARED from the issuer's own distribution schedule (quarterly, ex-dates in late Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec for TQQQ) and never computed or fetched. REFRESH EACH PHYSICAL SYMBOL'S BLOCK QUARTERLY: a span past `declared_through` refuses entry (dividend_calendar_lapsed) rather than assuming itself dividend-free, so a lapsed table stops entries loudly, by design. The example ships TQQQ declared through August only — August sits between the June and September distributions — so the first refresh is due before mid-September entries; fill in the September ex-date from the issuer page when you do.

TQQQ._source: ProShares own distribution schedule (proshares.com/resources/distributions/distribution-schedule), verified 2026-08-24: Q3 ex 9/23 payable 9/29, Q4 ex 12/23 payable 12/30, plus the POTENTIAL excise-tax distribution ex 12/31 payable 1/7/2027 (included deliberately -- refusing a week that might carry an ex-date is the safe direction). Cross-checked against an independent aggregator, which agreed on 9/23; this module's docs record that aggregators disagree by a day, so the issuer page is the authority and a second source is the check on it. DECLARED, never fetched -- nothing on a loop path may touch the network. Refresh by hand from the issuer page before an entry can span past declared_through; a lapse stops entries loudly, by design.

_source_note: stream_cache_db overrides the shared stream cache path; null means the suite default (~/.cherrypick/data/marketdata/stream_cache.db). This module is a pure READ-ONLY consumer of that cache — its two expirations are served by the streamer's `expirations` request field, and its deep strikes by the `window_hints` field, both declared automatically every tick.
_dte_note: The short lands on the soonest Friday with DTE in [short_dte_min, short_dte_max] (~7 days); the long on the Friday in [long_dte_min, long_dte_max] nearest long_dte_target (~21 days). The short window is deliberately at least as wide as the 7-day weekly spacing (5-11) so every weekday finds a qualifying Friday — narrower windows leave gaps on some weekdays. Computed from the calendar, asserted against the cache — never nearest-matched from the chain.
_selection_note: 2026-08-23 redesign. LONG: long_delta_min/long_delta_max define a DELTA BAND (default 0.85-0.90, not a floor) — the candidate whose delta falls in the band, nearest the band's midpoint, wins; a tie prefers the higher strike. With no greeks on file the candidate falls back to the pre-redesign heuristic (highest strike whose extrinsic is at most max_long_extrinsic per share) and the row records long_selected_by='extrinsic' so degraded entries stay excludable; a KNOWN delta outside the band is simply excluded, never laundered through the fallback. allow_extrinsic_fallback (default true) gates that degrade — set false to require a real delta on every candidate. SHORT: no yield floor and no ITM-only restriction any more — the short is the strike NEAREST spot, whichever side it lands on (ties prefer the ITM side). This can leave the short OTM; the worksheet math floors short_intrinsic at 0 in that case.
_management_note: The default control exit HOLDS the position to the short's own expiration and then closes both legs together (`short_expiration`) — no more early tv-exhaustion trigger, no more roll book, no more breach special case (the short can legitimately sit OTM by construction). tv_close_threshold and the new tv_managed_exit boolean remain as a live, advisor-tunable escape hatch back to the pre-redesign early-exit behavior: set only through an advised:control row's frozen advice_params overlay, never through this file, so the suite can run hold-to-expiry vs. early-tv-exit as a paper A/B. assignment_exposure_tv: marks with short extrinsic under this are flagged assignment-exposed — pure telemetry bounding what unmodelled early assignment could have touched. disposition_time is when delivered shares are covered and orphan longs sold the session after a settlement. exec_window_start gates ALL management action until the open stabilizes; max_leg_spread_pct is the is-this-mark-actionable bar (deep-ITM spreads are the module's known risk #2 — the attempts table measures how often this refuses).
_window_note: deep_window_pct bounds the entry snapshot's quote fetch: strikes in [spot*(1-deep_window_pct), spot*1.02]. The 85-90-delta long (2026-08-23 redesign) sits much closer to spot than the old ~99-delta design, so this dropped from 0.45 to 0.20 — via stream_window's window_hints, this is what makes the module's long-leg quotes exist at all.
_books_note: Single book since the 2026-08-23 redesign (the old keltner/roll books and the TNA/UPRO symbols are retired): `control` is mechanical entry whenever the (symbol, book) slot is free, hold to the short's own expiration, close both legs together, never roll. The `advised:control` synthetic twin (see the advice block below) is the only other row that can appear, and only when the advisor has admitted params for the session.
_stream_window_note: How wide an ATM window this module asks the producer for (window_hints). base_width mirrors the streamer's own default; the structural need is computed from the cached chain (strikes down to spot*(1-deep_window_pct) plus margin) and flies-style escalation on no_deep_itm_long / missing_leg_quotes refusals rides on top, decaying when quiet. The union across modules takes the max per symbol, so this can never narrow anyone else.
_tastytrade_costs_note: Overrides for the shared cost model (cherrypick.core.fees.DEFAULT_COSTS): slippage_frac_of_spread, slippage_cap_frac_of_mid, commissions. Empty means the suite defaults. The per-symbol pieces are automatic and this is the one place TQQQ and XSP genuinely differ in the fee stack: TQQQ is an ETF and is off the broad-based index exchange-fee schedule entirely, while XSP IS a broad-based index option and is looked up on cherrypick.core.fees.INDEX_EXCHANGE_FEE_PER_CONTRACT by symbol (currently $0.00/contract under 10 contracts/leg — the same number as the ETF default today, but wired through the index schedule rather than an ETF exemption, so a future rate change there reaches XSP automatically). Every ITM expiry costs the $5 settlement/assignment event regardless of symbol; only TQQQ's physical assignments add the SEC/FINRA pass-throughs on the share side (XSP never reaches that path).
advice_header: ===== the advised book (paper only, off by default) =====
_advice_note: When enabled AND the suite's advisor covers this module (advisor.modules.pmcc in the orchestrator config — both switches must agree), the session's admitted advice opens an `advised:control` book beside control, with the admitted params FROZEN on each row at entry and restated through management.effective_params at every later tick. base_book must be 'control' — it is the only book left. The one thing worth advising right now is the hold-to-expiry vs. early-tv-exit experiment: tv_managed_exit flips the exit rule, tv_close_threshold tunes the early-exit trigger when it does.
live_header: ===== live gate (placeholder — see the module CLAUDE.md's Live-trading prerequisites) =====
_live_note: This module has NO live loop, no order-placement code, and no live account designation. `enabled` exists only so the suite's config/console surfaces can read a real gate for this module instead of reporting an absent one as 'unknown' — flipping it to true does nothing until a live loop is built, and post-assignment management plus a calculated ex-div decision (the module CLAUDE.md's prerequisites) land first. Guarded the same as every other live gate: hand-edit only, never through the settings surface.
